clue.text: Mischievous type has fool replaced at the start

indicators.note: the opening letter of the fool word is swapped for another, which the clue leaves the solver to find

parts.note: a donkey is a stupid person, a fool

explanation.surface: A prankster has had the household fool swapped out for someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced at the start' changes the D of DONKEY; the new letter M is not clued, so the definition must confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky, playful child is often called a little monkey, a mischievous type.

clue.text: Bungled, in wearing fur?

definitions.meaning: dressed in a muff, the fur tube for warming the hands

explanation.definitionFit: Muffed means fumbled; whimsically it also describes someone wearing a muff of fur.

clue.text: Person ultimately overseeing good input to pilot

definitions.text: Person ultimately overseeing good input to pilot

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, overseeing, the rest
only the last letter of the word person is taken
a letter is put into the pilot word

parts.note: an aviator is a pilot

explanation.surface: A crew member who directs useful input to the pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives N; 'input to' puts G into AVIATOR; 'overseeing' puts N on top. The whole clue describes the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator is the crew member who guides the pilot with directions.

clue.text: Supply the ultimate in rude jokes? Just the one

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: a single joke, one witty remark, is a quip

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the very rudest jokes, but only one is given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ultimate in' gives E, the last letter of 'rude'.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to supply with what is needed, a verb meaning provide.

clue.text: Giant wastage in north African food — only half used

indicators.note: the wastage word goes inside what is left of the food, so 'in' signals a container
only one of the two halves of the food word is kept, the front half

parts.note: couscous is a steamed semolina dish from North Africa
wastage is loss

explanation.surface: Lots of waste in a North African dish, only half of which is eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half used' keeps the first half of the dish's name; 'in' then signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A colossus is a huge statue, hence any giant figure or thing.

clue.text: Gradually ease temptation to send flying

indicators.note: sending the letters flying scatters them into a new order

explanation.surface: Resist temptation slowly and kick it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to send flying' rearranges the fourteen letters of EASE TEMPTATION.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means little by little, in stages, which is a gradual pace.

clue.text: Box in odd Scottish players

indicators.note: the box goes inside the Scottish word

parts.note: orra is a Scots word meaning odd or spare
a chest is a box

explanation.surface: A box placed among some eccentric Scottish players.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scots dialect word for odd is a fair test only because the clue flags it as Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a group of musicians, players of instruments.

clue.text: Keen types sent up to university are in confusion

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: fans are keen enthusiasts

explanation.surface: Enthusiastic students sent off to university are bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns FANS into SNAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Snafu, military slang for a chaotic foul-up, describes a state of disorder.

clue.text: Quick fare available here from new cab-ranks

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fast food can be bought at the newly built taxi ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CABRANKS. 'fare' looks like a taxi charge but means food.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack bar is a counter selling quick light meals.

clue.text: Top job should be dispatched quickly

definitions.meaning: a best-class position, a first-rate post
mail paid at the faster rate, sent for next-day delivery

explanation.definitionFit: A post is a job, so a first-rate one is top; it is also the Royal Mail's priority postal service.

clue.text: Beloved pet that attracts lots of money

definitions.meaning: a pet that is loved most of all, a preferred one
in betting, the runner backed most heavily by punters

explanation.definitionFit: A favourite is both the best-loved one and the horse most heavily backed in a race.

clue.text: Girl caught another

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Lara is another girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is caught by somebody else.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara is a female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Regularly engage clutch component

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one, from the next word

explanation.surface: A driver is told to keep engaging the clutch.
explanation.walkthrough: The motoring surface makes 'clutch' a car pedal; here it is a nest of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A clutch is a set of eggs laid together, so one egg is a component of it.

clue.text: She's put back dodgy transfer deal, literally

definitions.text: She's put back dodgy transfer deal, literally

parts.words: She's put back dodgy transfer deal, literally
parts.note: shifting blame onto someone else is a dodgy transfer; in old poker a marker passed round showed who dealt, so passing it literally transferred the deal

explanation.surface: Someone has pushed back a shady deal involving a transfer.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker a knife or marker (the 'buck') sat before the dealer and moved on to the next player, so the idiom literally means handing on the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to shift responsibility to another, and comes from moving the dealer's marker in poker.

clue.text: Still at breaking point with spasm

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point

indicators.note: the word at is broken up and its two letters rearranged

parts.note: a tic is a nervous spasm

explanation.surface: Stillness at breaking point, accompanied by a spasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges the two letters of 'at'; 'point' is a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means not moving, still.

clue.text: Trouble nurse about ten or eleven in Yorkshire, for example

definitions.text: ten or eleven in Yorkshire, for example

indicators.note: the nurse word goes around the trouble word

parts.note: a tender is one who tends or nurses
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Nursing a sick team member in Yorkshire, around ten or eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a county cricket team; its numbers ten and eleven bat last. The numbers look like clock times.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a tail-ender is one of the weak batsmen at the bottom of the order.

clue.text: Flower is eradicated from country after exercise

indicators.note: the country part follows the exercise part

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

indicators.note: the word is is wiped out of the country's name

parts.note: Tunisia is a North African country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flower has been wiped out of a country after some exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is eradicated from' removes the clue's own word 'is' from the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The petunia is a garden plant grown for its trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: About to break into song on Germany's capital city

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the next
the about word goes inside the song word

parts.note: a number is a song
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the capital, first, letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A singer is about to burst into song about Germany's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Berlin but gives G, the first letter of Germany's.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuremberg is a city in Bavaria, Germany.

clue.text: The time of our lives, a cosmic experience

definitions.text: The time of our lives, a cosmic experience

parts.words: The time of our lives, a cosmic experience
parts.note: the era we live in, defined by travel beyond Earth's atmosphere

explanation.surface: Having the time of our lives on a mind-blowing trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cosmic experience' reads as slang for something amazing, but means literal outer-space exploration.
explanation.definitionFit: The modern era of space exploration is the one we live in.

clue.text: Suite of mine with a painting that's framed

indicators.note: the painting sits inside the mine word as if in a frame

parts.note: a pit is a mine
art is painting
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suite of rooms in a mine, with a framed picture on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suite' looks like hotel rooms but is a musical suite.
explanation.definitionFit: A partita is a musical suite, a set of instrumental pieces.

clue.text: Seabird, devouring most of another, leaves vessel?

indicators.note: the first bird eats the second, so holds it inside

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

indicators.note: the last letter of the second bird is dropped

parts.note: an auk is another seabird

explanation.surface: One seabird eats most of another and flies off from a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims AUK to AU, which TERN is 'devouring'. 'leaves' looks like a verb but means tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea urn is a large container in which tea leaves are brewed.

clue.text: Sauce right inside 29? On the contrary

indicators.note: the right letter goes inside the sauce

parts.note: pesto is a basil sauce

explanation.surface: A sauce gets the right ingredient inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 across means 'slowly' in music; the contrary is a very fast tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto, very fast, is the opposite tempo marking to a slow one.

clue.text: Made up, getting minute folds covered over

indicators.note: the covering word takes in, gets, the other pieces

parts.note: coated means covered over
pens are folds for sheep

explanation.surface: Someone is made up after receiving some tiny folds that were covered over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up' means made amends, not invented or wearing makeup.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensated means made up for a loss, recompensed.

clue.text: In 2001, one initially cast as ape

indicators.note: 'In' here means placed within, so the numeral for one is set inside the Roman year

parts.note: MMI is 2001 in Roman numerals
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: In the film 2001, someone was cast as an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at the apes of the film 2001; MMI is the year in Roman numerals, with I put 'In' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape is to copy, as a mimic does.

clue.text: Runs in unqualified fear

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the other word

parts.note: dead means absolute, unqualified, as in dead certain
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs in fear without qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear, apprehension.

clue.text: Core of metamorphic soil material

indicators.note: the centre of the word holds the letters needed

explanation.surface: A geology note about the heart of metamorphic rock in soil.
explanation.walkthrough: MOR is the middle three letters of 'metamorphic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mor is a layer of acid humus found on top of some forest soils.

clue.text: Yours truly into endless Hardy with Browning?

indicators.note: the self word goes into the trimmed name
the name loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: yours truly means the writer, me

explanation.surface: The writer slips between the poets Hardy and Browning.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy and Browning look like the two poets, but a Browning is a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying a Browning pistol or rifle means being armed.

clue.text: They measure in millimetres or these after conversion

indicators.note: conversion changes the letters into a new order

parts.note: mm is the abbreviation for millimetres
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instruments measure in millimetres, or else these after a unit conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: The metric surface hides that millimetres gives only its abbreviation to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohmmeters are instruments that measure electrical resistance.

clue.text: Scraps forces regularly infiltrated by Communist Party

indicators.note: the two letters are spaced evenly through the forces word, not side by side
letters get into the forces word from outside

parts.note: exerts means forces, as in exerts pressure
C is a common abbreviation for Communist
P is the abbreviation for Party

explanation.surface: Military forces are steadily infiltrated by Communist Party agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infiltrated by' and 'regularly' put C and P into EXERTS at even spacing: EX-C-ER-P-TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Excerpts are extracts or snippets, scraps taken from a longer work.

clue.text: Slowly our years have a cost, as we change

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the years of our era
an agio is the premium charged when exchanging currency

explanation.surface: Getting older costs us something as we change.
explanation.walkthrough: An agio is the fee paid when changing one currency for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction meaning play slowly.
